tasks.title: Dust and Young Stars in Star-forming Galaxies
tasks.statement: As a by-product of the star-forming process in a galaxy, interstellar dust can significantly absorb stellar light in ultraviolet (UV) and optical bands, and then re-emit in far-infrared (FIR), which corresponds to a wavelength range of 10-300 µm.

u = f_\lambda \Delta\lambda)

Table 1 presents the observed IR photometry results for a z = 6.60 galaxy called CR7. Plot the AB magnitude of CR7 versus the logarithm of the rest-frame wavelength on graph paper and labelled as Figure 1.
parts.reference: Equation (3): 2 marks; Correct wavelengths: 2 marks; Figure: 8 marks.

parts.question: Calculate CR7’s UV slope, plot the best-fit UV continuum on Figure 1 and make a comparison with the results you obtained in (D1.1.1). Is it dustier than the typical galaxy in (D1.1.1)? Please answer with [YES] or [NO]. (Hint: Express m_{AB} as a function of \lambda and m_{1600}, where m_{1600} is the AB magnitude at \lambda_0 = 160 nm (1600 Å))
parts.reference: beta: 3 marks; Comparison / [NO]: 2 marks. Grading standard of Figure 1: (1) Figure large enough (>50%); (2) horizontal axis rest-frame wavelength in log scale; (3) vertical axis AB magnitude plotted reversely; (4) Ticks properly labeled; (5) Data points and best-fit plotted properly; (6) Error bars presented properly.

parts.question: Based on the data given in Table 2, plot the IRX − \beta diagram on graph paper and labelled as Figure 2 and find a linear fit to the data. Write down your best-fit equation (i.e. IRX = a \cdot \beta + b) by the side of your diagram.
parts.reference: Equation (5): 1 mark; Equation (6): 3 marks; Figure 2: 10 marks. Grading standard of Figure 2: (1) Figure large enough; (2) axes linear scale; (3) Ticks properly labeled; (4) Data points and best-fit plotted properly; (5) Best-fit equation noted correctly.

parts.question: Quantify the dispersion (in ‘units’ of dex, where for example, \log_{10} 9 - \log_{10} 4 = 5 \text{ dex}) between the observed IRX_obs and predicted IRX_pred using the provided equation.
Express A_{1600} as a function of IRX.

Based on Table 2 data and the function of A_{1600} (IRX) you derived above, plot the A_{1600} − \beta diagram on graph paper and label it as Figure 3 and find a linear fit to the data. Write down your best-fit equation (i.e. A_{1600} = a_\nu \cdot \beta + b_\nu) by the side of your diagram.
parts.reference: Equation (10): 2 marks; Figure 3: 10 marks. Grading standard of Figure 3: (1) Figure large enough; (2) axes linear scale; (3) Ticks properly labeled; (4) Data points and best-fit function plotted properly; (5) Best-fit equation noted correctly.

parts.question: If your linear model in (D1.3.2) is correct, what is the expected UV continuum slope \beta_0 of a dust-free galaxy?
Calculate the IRX of CR7. Is it an upper limit or lower limit?

Is the current observation long enough to show any deviation of CR7 from the IRX−\beta relationship you just derived in the local universe? Please answer with [YES] or [NO] on the summary answer sheet, give the IRX difference and show the working used to calculate it on the answer sheet.
parts.reference: Equation (14): 2 marks; two IRX difference: 2 marks; [NO]: 2 marks.

tasks.title: Compact Object in a Binary System
tasks.statement: Astronomers discovered an extraordinary binary system in the constellation of Auriga during the course of the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). In these questions, you will try to analyse the data and recreate their discovery for yourself.

parts.question: Use the data and a simple linear model to obtain an initial estimate of the apparent maximum acceleration of the star: a_{app} = \Delta v / \Delta t, unit: km s-1 day-1
parts.reference: 6 marks for the calculation using Equation (15).

parts.question: Now use the data to obtain an initial estimate of the mass of its unseen companion.
parts.reference: 4 marks for M_2 within 0.5 M_\odot ~ 3 M_\odot with clear and proper assumption (5 marks).

parts.question: Plot the diagram of RV variation (measured with TRES) versus time on your graph paper and label it as Figure 4. Draw a suitable sinusoidal function to fit the given data. Estimate the orbital period (P_orb) and radial velocity semi-amplitude (K) from your plot.
parts.reference: Figure grading: (1) Figure large enough; (2) axes linear scale; (3) Ticks properly labeled; (4) Data points and sinusoidal function plotted properly. 2 marks for each parameter (P_orb and K).

parts.question: If the star is moving in a circular orbit, calculate the minimum value of the orbital radius (r_orb) of the star in units of both R_\odot and au.
parts.reference: 4 marks for the calculation of minimum orbital radius.

parts.question: The mass function of a binary system is defined as f(M_1, M_2) = (M_2 \sin i_{orb})^3 / (M_1 + M_2)^2. Calculate the mass function of this system in units of M_\odot.
parts.reference: Equation (21), (22): 2 marks respectively; Equation (23) and the result: 3 marks.

parts.question: Calculate the luminosity (L_1, in unit of L_\odot ), radius (R_1, in unit of R_\odot ), sine of the inclination angle (sin i), as well as mass (M_1, in unit of M_\odot ) of the visible star. Please include the uncertainty in your results.
parts.reference: For each quantity (sin i, R_1, M_1, L_1): deduction: 2 marks; exact value: 1 mark; uncertainty: 1 mark.

parts.question: Choose the correct type of this star from the following options: (1) Blue Giant (2) Yellow main sequence star (3) Red Giant (4) Red main sequence star (5) White Dwarf.

Based on the mass function f(M_1, M_2) of the binary system, plot the rough relationship of M_2 (as vertical axis) and M_1 (as horizontal axis) on your graph paper and label it as Figure 5. Plot the most probable relation (by using \sin i), upper limit (with \sin i + \Delta \sin i) and lower limit (with \sin i - \Delta \sin i) derived in (D2.3.1).
parts.reference: Grading standard of Figure 5: (1) Figure large enough; (2) axes linear scale; (3) Ticks properly labeled; (4) Three mass functions plotted properly with labels; (5) Vertical shadowed region plotted correctly; (6) Two horizontal dashed lines plotted at correct positions.

parts.question: Draw a vertical shadowed region of [M_1 - \Delta M_1, M_1 + \Delta M_1], as well as two horizontal dashed lines showing the maximum mass of the white dwarf and neutron star, on your Figure 5. What is the possible mass of the invisible companion, and what kind of celestial object could it be?
